structured_output.summary: The source changes are almost identical to the reference. `played_colors_by_name` builds the chunked `name -> frozenset` table with `counted` dropped, and `played_colors_of` reads `(colors, cards_seen)` from it. `live_opponent_colors` now composes the two; it collects the names into a set before the two calls, so a generator argument still works. The route drops its two private copies and the `COLOR_ORDER` import. The author found `card_colors_by_name` already in use, chose `played_*` names (the same as the reference) and said so in the report. Docstrings stay true: the shared rule (supertype test, unreadable JSON, rule 4) now sits on the bulk function, and `live_opponent_colors` keeps the view-arithmetic and distinct-names points. The equality test was replaced with an identity test, which fails on revert (`revert_py` exit 2). An unreadable-JSON test was added because the existing live-read tests lacked that case. A 602-name chunk test puts a known card in each chunk. The `docs/current-match.md` sentence is still true, so leaving that doc alone was right. Ruff is clean and the full suite passes. The report is accurate, lists its decisions and names what it did not verify.
